newsitem.title: UK: Sterling strides ahead after bullish Clarke speech.
newsitem.headline: Sterling strides ahead after bullish Clarke speech.

text.p: Sterling made further strong gains against the mark and the dollar in active European trade amid a positive market reaction to what looks to be new-found unity in the ruling Conservative party.
Dealers said sentiment was bolstered by the unexpectedly strong performance of Chancellor Kenneth Clarke in a speech on Thursday to the Conservative Party annual conference.
"It didn't take much of a trigger (to improve sterling sentiment)," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International in London.

Sterling broke through 2.40 marks in early business and pushed on at 0818 GMT to 2.4078/83, compared with 2.3940/45 late Thursday in Europe. It also rose strongly against the dollar to $1.5728/35 at 0818 GMT compared with $1.5652/59.

Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank, said the break of 2.4020 marks was very important for the bullish sterling scenario and the pound should now target the 2.4090/4130 range and further to 2.42.
Clarke's speech papered over months of squabbling over European and monetary union (EMU) which had until now made Conservative victory in another general election a bad bet.
"They have certainly had a better conference than the market thought they would have," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy.

Newspapers hailed Clarke's speech as a triumph, and the Times said it was a "barnstorming" performance which vanquished his Euro-sceptic foes to the right of the party and strengthened his authority as Chancellor.
Dealers said an article in Friday's Times predicting a rise in sterling also helped boost sentiment.
"The article in The Times seems to have given Far Eastern players a chance to push sterling/mark up a quick 30 to 40 points," said a UK bank dealer.

The article said the winner of next year's election, at the moment heavily tipped by pollsters to be the the opposition Labour Party, would be dogged with a strong currency which would be a major headache for exporters.
It said sterling would be boosted by a package of tax cuts and public spending plans which is likely to be announced in Clarke's final pre-election budget, to be unveiled next month.
"The market overemphasised the (Times) article but it highlights that sterling sentiment is favourable," said Lyons.
The market will be looking out for more strong political medicine in a speech at 1020 GMT from Major, who is expected to stress the message of Conservative Party unity.
Dealers said sterling would continue to see some follow- through in Europe, but would settle at around 2.4050.
They said the pound was further supported by the view that it had been undervalued in recent months.

Moreover, sterling is being dragged up in line with EMU convergance trades amid speculation that the lira, markka and possibly the Swedish crown were preparing to join the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM).

On top of this, the pound is seen as being a safe-haven from any European turmoil that might result if the process of monetary union begins to crumble because most traders do not believe that Britain will be in the first EMU group in 1999.
